_comment: Technical Design v0.38–v0.39's Setting Pack and Player Interface: the player's words. Command names and hints, refusal reasons, example lines, and every label the player screen shows. Code fills the {named} placeholders and writes none of these words itself (CC-20261111-08, #61; the screen's labels CC-20261111-09, #62).

commands._comment: Keyed by the game's action. `name` is what the player types; `usage` shows its arguments; `hint` is the command menu's one line.

bribe.name: /bribe
bribe.hint: Hand the guest you're alone with n {currency}.

repay.name: /repay
repay.hint: Renounce one French pension, your own or a relative's, for {amount} {currency}.

conclude.name: /conclude
conclude.hint: Note privately what you've worked out. Only your latest counts.

refusals._comment: Sent to the player alone, with the reason. Mechanics' reasons: mistimed, not allowed, can't afford it, unknown guest, not present.
refusals.cant_afford: You can't afford that: you have {purse} {currency}.
refusals.not_positive: Name a number of {currency} above nothing.
refusals.message_used: You've spoken your piece this turn. You can speak again next turn.
refusals.message_held: Your words are waiting to be spoken.
refusals.pension_refused: You hold no pension you could renounce for {holder}, or can't pay it back.
refusals.end_mistimed: There's no private conversation for you to end.

acts._comment: Midnight: why the acts were refused (Mechanics, Murder Round).
acts.count: Choose exactly the number of acts you may take tonight.
acts.self: You can't take an act on yourself.
acts.same_guest: Each of your acts must name a different guest.

refusals.note_too_long: That note is {length} characters; keep it to {max}.
refusals.note_guest: A note can be about guests at this party only.

briefingHeadings._comment: Headings in the Characters doc's briefings that the screen looks for (the errand card shows its section). Not shown as words.

screen._comment: The player screen's labels (TD v0.39–v0.47, The screen).
screen.title: Gonfaloniere

input.placeholder: Say something. @ addresses a guest; / opens the commands.
input._examplesComment: Interface v0.5: the placeholder carries the example, one line with an @ and a /, rotated, using only commands allowed right now. `action` is the command's action (as in commands); {command} is its name and {guest} a guest the player could address. With none allowed, `placeholder` shows.

examples.text: Speak as your character would… “@{guest} A word, by the window?” or “{command} @{guest} 2”
Speak as your character would… “@{guest} My family has long memories, and longer purses.” or “{command}”
Speak as your character would… “@{guest} I'd rather speak of this somewhere quieter.” or “{command} @{guest}”
Speak as your character would… “@{guest} You seem very sure of that. Who told you?” or “{command} what you've worked out”

input.used: You've spoken your piece this turn.
input.held: Your words will be spoken at the next pause.
input.waiting: The company waits for you: speak, or pass.
input.answering: {name} has addressed you: answer, or pass.
input.closing: {name} has ended the conversation: a last word, or pass.
input.pastPlaceholder: You're reading an earlier stage. Write here if you like: nothing is sent until you're back in the current stage.
input.pastWaiting: The current stage is waiting for you. Return when you're ready.

seat.inviteeTitle: The conversation with {initiator} is over. Where do you go?
seat.loneTitle: You're left alone. Join a group.

midnight.title: Midnight
midnight.introTwo: Choose one or two acts for tonight.
midnight.extraNote: Optional: leave it empty if you don't want it.
midnight.extraSame: Your extra act must name a different guest from your other act.

death.you: You have died. From here you watch, as the city does.

end.title: The evening is over
end.dead: You did not survive the night.

errandCard._comment: TD v0.47, the errand card: under the errand's text, one line saying what finishing it earns. `reward` with the run's plot_reward on (the rules primer's terms), `noReward` with it off, as in the mini-game. After the errand's check, {plot_status} replaces the line.
errandCard.title: Your errand
errandCard.reward: Finish it before the last council before midnight for one extra act at midnight: a second kill, guard, or watch, on a different guest. No one else is told.
errandCard.noReward: Errands earn no extra act tonight.

midnightLine._comment: Interface v0.8, the midnight line in the sheet: the act every guest has at midnight, then with plot_reward on the extra act the errand can earn, in the errand card's terms. After the errand's check, `earned` if the extra act is the player's; otherwise the second line goes.
midnightLine.reward: +1 if you finish your errand before the last council

stageBar._comment: Interface v0.5, the stage bar: one line for each stage, keyed by the stage's name as block 5 gives it (in-world-names.json's phase labels). A stage without a line here shows its name alone.

descriptions.The guests' arrival: The guests come in and form their first groups.
descriptions.The first round of mingling, early: Talk in small groups; move, or call someone aside.
descriptions.The first round of mingling, midway: The round goes on, and the groups shift.
descriptions.The first round of mingling, late: The round's last stretch before midnight.
descriptions.Midnight: Each guest acts alone, in secret.

pastStage.heading: Earlier: {stage}
pastStage.empty: Nothing reached you in this stage.

hints._comment: Hover explanations (TD v0.40, The screen), on hover and keyboard focus. Plain words for someone new to the game.
hints.switch: Turn these explanations on or off. This browser remembers your choice.
hints.sheet: Your character: your purse, the French pensions you hold, and how many times tonight you've drawn someone aside for a private word.
hints.errand: What you came to do tonight. It stays here so you don't lose sight of it. Once it has been checked, the result appears here too.
hints.errandReward: What you came to do tonight. It stays here so you don't lose sight of it. Finish it before the last council before midnight, and you get one extra act at midnight, a second kill, guard, or watch on a different guest, that no one else is told about. Once it has been checked, the result appears here.
hints.errandNoReward: What you came to do tonight. It stays here so you don't lose sight of it. Tonight, errands earn no extra act at midnight, so finishing it is for its own sake.
hints.trackDeadline: Your errand's deadline: finish it before this for an extra act at midnight.
hints.midnightExtra: The extra act your errand earned you. No one else is told of it. It's yours to use or leave: it must name a different guest from your other act, and you can't guard yourself.
hints.here: The room: the guests with you, then everyone else as they stand right now. You can see who is with whom, never what they say.
hints.briefing: Your briefing: who you are, what you know, and what you want. Only you can see it.
hints.rules: The rules of the evening, as every guest has them: one button per section.
hints.header: Who you're with now, in the current stage.
hints.earlier: Conversations you were part of earlier in this stage. Click one to read it again; click again to fold it away. Earlier stages are in the bar above.
hints.input: Type what your character says, up to {max} characters. Start with @ to speak to one guest, or / for a command.
hints.mention: Speak to one guest: choose who your next line is for. Everyone present still hears it.
hints.commands: Commands: actions such as paying, borrowing, or repaying, instead of words.
hints.speak: Say your line to the conversation. You can press Enter instead.
hints.do: Carry out the command in the box. It's an action, not something you say.
hints.pass: Say nothing this time. The conversation moves on.
hints.end: End this private conversation. The other guest has a last word, then it closes.
hints.talkingTo: The guest you're talking with. Everything shown here is what anyone at the party knows about them.
hints.move: Your chance to move. Stay where you are, walk over to another guest's group, or call a guest aside for a private word.
hints.join: Walk over to another guest and join their group.
hints.colloquio: Draw a guest aside for a private conversation. Il Notaio notes it, and others may wonder why.
hints.seat: Your conversation is over. Choose where to go next.
hints.midnight: Choose what you do at midnight. No one sees your choice.
hints.confirm: Lock in your choice. It can't be changed afterwards.
hints.close: Close this and go back to the conversation.
hints.play: Start the evening as this guest.
hints.wait: Wait here until a seat opens in a group. You'll be offered one at the next chance.
hints.city: The city: what everyone in Florence knows, one entry per row, under its subject.
hints.web: The Web of Secrets: who is tied to whom, what you heard and saw of each guest, and your notes. Click the bar to slide it up or down.
hints.select: Select this guest, here and in the Web of Secrets: their public card shows on the right, their lines are highlighted, and earlier conversations they were in open up. Select again, or press Escape, to clear.
hints.loreLink: Something everyone in the city knows about. Opens it on the right.
hints.earlierLine: Open or fold this earlier conversation.
hints.deckCard: Click anywhere on the card, or press the right arrow, for the next topic.
hints.deckBack: Back to the previous topic. The left arrow works too.
hints.selected: The guest you selected. Everything shown is what anyone at the party knows about them.
hints.back: Back to what you were looking at before.
hints.openWeb: Open the Web of Secrets with this guest selected.
hints.notaioHint: Il Notaio's advice for the moment. Click to fold it away or bring it back.
hints.webNode: Select a guest. Select a second to see what passed between the two; a third replaces the older. The conversation shows the one you picked last.
hints.recordTab: What you heard the selected guests say, and what you saw of them, newest first. Only what you were there for.
hints.notesTab: Write a note on the selected guest or pair, or with no one selected, a free note. Below it, your notes, newest first: all of them with no one selected, or those on whoever is selected. Only you see your notes.
hints.noteText: Your note. No one else sees it, and no guest's mind is touched by it.
hints.noteSave: Keep this note. It stays with the game, even if you reload the page.
hints.conclude: Put this note in the message box as your conclusion: what you've worked out. Nothing counts until you press Do, and only your latest conclusion counts, so a new one replaces the last.
hints.concludeWaiting: Finish the choice in front of you first. Then you can make this note your conclusion.
hints.noteItem: Select the guest or pair this note is about: the list narrows to them, and the web highlights them.
hints.portrait: {name}. Click to select them, here and in the Web of Secrets.
hints.more: This column goes on below. Click to scroll down, or scroll as usual.
hints.key: The key to the lines: each kind of tie has its own colour and line style.
hints.keyType: Highlight every line of this kind across the web. Click again to clear.
hints.reading: Il Notaio's short reading of what you've heard and seen of the selected guests. It's one model's summary of your own record, and every quote is checked against it. He may still be wrong. Click it, or the lines behind it, to fold it to the foot of the column; click again to bring it back.
hints.faction: A faction: its guests sit together under its name.
hints.track: The evening's stages: filled ones are done, the long one is now, outlined ones are still to come.
hints.trackPast: {stage}: done. Click to read its conversations again. Nothing can be sent from there.
hints.trackNow: {stage}: now. Click to come back here from an earlier stage.
hints.trackNext: {stage}: still to come. It opens once it has happened.
hints.return: Back to the current stage. Your words stay in the box; nothing is sent until you press Speak or Do there. Enter does the same.
hints.pastStage: An earlier stage, read-only: every conversation you were in during it, in order.
hints.lookingAt: The guest you selected, over the one you're talking with. Everything shown is what anyone at the party knows about them.
hints.deselect: Stop looking at this guest, and go back to whoever you're talking with.
hints.backToTalk: Back to whoever you're talking with.
hints.resize: Drag to make this panel wider or narrower. This browser remembers the width.
hints.loreEntry: A lore entry you opened from a line. Back returns to what you were looking at.
hints.roomToken: {name}, in company. Click to select them.
hints.roomPair: {name}, in private. Click to select them.
hints.places: The places: every place in the house, always in the same order, and who is in each right now. Yours is marked, and a closed door marks a private conversation. You can see who is with whom, never what they say. Hover a place's name to read about it.
hints.placePrivate: Two guests have drawn aside here in private, behind a closed door. You can see who, never what they say.
hints.rulesSection: Open this section of the rules. Its × takes you back to all of them.
hints.rulesShrink: Back to all the sections of the rules.
hints.cityRow: Read this entry in full. The arrow at its top takes you back to the list.
hints.cityBack: Back to the list of everything the city knows.
hints.hideRight: Hide this panel, so the conversation has more room. A handle at the edge brings it back; this browser remembers your choice.
hints.showRight: Show the right panel again. While it's hidden, the guest you've selected shows here.
hints.glossary: The glossary: the evening's words from A to Z, each with a short definition, and a search box.
hints.glossarySearch: Type to narrow the glossary to the words that match.
hints.glossaryRules: Open the rules at the section behind this word.
hints.modalPrevious: The one before this. Click to slide back to it.
hints.modalNext: The next one along. Click to slide on to it.
hints.tourAgain: Take the tour of the screen again: one part at a time, with a word from Il Notaio on each.
hints.tourSkip: End the tour here. Show me around, at the top of this column, runs it again.
hints.openingSkip: Write out the whole story at once.

web.placeholder: What do you make of it?

places._comment: Interface v0.9, Left: The places, from the player's state's `places` (TD v0.49). Every place in setting.json's order; a row's heading is the place's name with its first letter capitalized. `yours` marks the player's own place, `private` names the closed-door mark on a place holding a Colloquio, and `quiet` stands in for the list outside a conversation (midnight, the ballot). `descriptions`: Lore's one-line description of each place (Lore v0.8, The Palazzo), shown on hovering its name, keyed by the place's name exactly as setting.json gives it.
places.title: The places

descriptions.the great hall: The main room, under painted beams, where the crowd gathers
descriptions.the window bay: A deep window seat at the great hall's far end, over the street
descriptions.the anteroom: At the top of the stair, where guests wait to be announced
descriptions.the loggia: An open arcade on the upper floor, overlooking the courtyard
descriptions.the courtyard: Below the loggia, around the well, open to the night sky
descriptions.the study: The host's small room of books and letters
descriptions.the painted room: Its walls frescoed with the months of the year
descriptions.the dining room: The long table, laid for the mourners' supper

placeLine._comment: Interface v0.9, the conversation line (the members line under the stage bar, and each earlier conversation's line), once the state has places (TD v0.49). {place} is the place's name as setting.json gives it, in a sentence as is; {others} the guests with the player, joined; {other} the Colloquio's other guest; {faction} the player's faction. Without places, `capannello`, `colloquio`, and `alone` above.

opening._comment: Interface v0.7, The Opening's controls and the choice at its end. Il Notaio's story itself is notaio.json's opening.

tour._comment: Interface v0.8, The Tour's controls. Its cards are notaio.json's tour.

glossary._comment: Interface v0.7, the glossary (Glossary Draft; v0.11's gloss on Il Notaio; v0.12's words). One entry per term: `text` is its plain definition, with every amount a {placeholder} filled from the game's tuning values (Mechanics, Tunable Values: {starting_florins}, {income}, {vote_price}, {pension_size}; {currency} is the setting's plural), never typed in. `fullGame`: marked † in the draft, left out of the mini-game. `rules`: the rules sections "More in the rules" opens, by title, the first the rules have. `match`: the words in a line that get the term's dotted underline (none for the midnight acts and Move, whose words are everyday ones). Not shown as the screen's own words: the server sends them filled (screen-info.ts).

entries.text: The secret vote that ends the evening. Every living guest casts one vote for any living guest, and may buy extra votes for that guest at {vote_price} {currency} each. Most votes wins; Il Notaio names only the winner.
Hand {currency} to the guest you're alone with in a Colloquio. Whatever they promise in return is up to them.
Go on France's payroll: take one payroll payment of {pension_size} {currency} from the Embassy's treasury. Medici and Pazzi only.
The one living guest each of the two great houses, Medici and Pazzi, puts forward for Gonfaloniere.
An open conversation of two to four guests. Anyone may join while it has room, and only those in it hear what's said.
A private conversation between two guests. No one else can join or hear. Calling one uses your move, and the guest you call can't refuse, but everyone sees the two of you slip away.
Privately record what you've worked out, for an errand that asks you to find something out. Only your latest conclusion counts.
A private meeting of your own faction. Nothing is shared unless someone says it aloud.
The friars' faction. They can't go on France's payroll. They win if the guest elected Gonfaloniere has repented.
Your character's own task tonight, in your briefing. Your errand card says what finishing it earns.
The evening's money. Everyone starts with {starting_florins} and receives {income} at the start of each round of mingling. Purses are private.
France's faction. It keeps the treasury that pays France's payroll, and knows who is on it. It wins if anyone in the elected candidate's family is on France's payroll.

Taking a payroll payment, {pension_size} {currency} from the French Embassy, puts a guest on France's payroll. If anyone in the winning candidate's family is still on it at the ballot, France wins. Who is on it is private unless someone tells.
The office the evening decides: the head of Florence's government. Only a Medici or a Pazzi can stand.
A midnight act. A guest guarded by two or more others survives an attack.
Italian for “the notary”: the one who records the evening. He notes who joins, leaves, and slips away, and announces what all the city hears. He belongs to no faction.
A midnight act. It's carried out unless the killer was watched by two or more guests, or the target guarded by two or more. Killers are never named.
One of the two great houses, competing for Gonfaloniere. They win if their candidate is elected, unrepentant, with no one in the family on France's payroll.
When each living guest secretly chooses one act: kill, guard, or watch, each on a different guest. Il Notaio then announces who died, never who killed them.
Your turn to change company, when it comes: stay, join another guest's group, or call a Colloquio.
The other great house, competing for Gonfaloniere, on the same terms as the Medici.
Pay back one payroll payment, yours or a relative's, by returning {pension_size} {currency}, any time before the ballot. Private.
A candidate's public confession during the speeches. It can't be taken back, and it makes the Dominicans' win their own.
Open play, when guests form groups, move, and call Colloquios.
If the ballot ties, one fresh vote among the tied guests, with no buying. A second tie is decided by lot.
Each candidate addresses the city, and others may speak. The only time a candidate can repent.
A midnight act. A guest watched by two or more others can't carry out their kill. The watchers learn nothing.
Your record of who is tied to whom, what you've heard of each guest, and your notes. The bar at the bottom of the screen.
